title: Regular nodal trait surface and Hartogs after flat base change
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $\pi$ a uniformizer, $B=A[s,t]/(st-\pi)$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $o=V(s,t)$, and $U=D(s)\cup D(t)$. Then $X$ is an integral Noetherian regular scheme of dimension two [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and $\dim\mathcal O_{X,o}=2$. For every flat morphism $f:T\to X$ [def-weil-flat-morphism], put $U_T=T\times_XU$ and let $j_T:U_T\hookrightarrow T$ be the open inclusion. The canonical map $\mathcal O_T\to(j_T)_*\mathcal O_{U_T}$ is an isomorphism. Consequently, for finite locally free $\mathcal O_T$-modules $M,N$ [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], restriction induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_T}(M,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{U_T}}(M|_{U_T},N|_{U_T})$; for every affine $T$-scheme $Z\to T$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism], restriction induces a bijection between its sections over $T$ and over $U_T$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $T$ is imposed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf, Section 2, Claim 2, printed p.2 (regularity and functions). Flat-base version: on affine charts tensor the exact Laurent two-open equalizer for B with a flat B-algebra. This does not use completion.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-dvr-binomial-local-geometry with $R=A$, $x=s$, $y=t$, and $e=1$. Since $\pi=st$ in $B$, its distinguished ideal $(\pi,s,t)$ is exactly $(s,t)$, so its point $o$ and its complementary opens are the ones here. The lemma gives Noetherianity, regularity at $o$, regularity on both complementary opens, the bound $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}\le2$ at every point, and equality at $o$. By the local-ring characterization of regular schemes, $X$ is regular; the supremum-of-local-dimensions theorem gives $\dim X=2$. The binomial Laurent normal-form lemma applies because a DVR is a domain and $\pi\ne0$; its injection $B\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}(A)(T)$ makes $B$ a domain. The spectrum-of-domain theorem therefore makes $X$ integral.

proof.text:
The binomial Laurent normal-form lemma embeds $B_s$ and $B_t$ into $K(T)$, where $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and identifies their intersection with the image of $B$. Their further localizations $B_{st}$ embed there as well: localization of any subring of a field at a nonzero element is represented by fractions in that field, and $s,t\ne0$. Consequently
$$0\longrightarrow B\xrightarrow{b\mapsto(b,b)}B_s\oplus B_t\xrightarrow{(a,b)\mapsto a-b}B_{st}$$
is exact: injectivity follows from the embedding of $B$, and a pair in the kernel is a common element of $B_s$ and $B_t$, hence comes from exactly one element of $B$. No surjectivity onto $B_{st}$ is asserted.

source.place: Elementary intersection-to-kernel argument from the cited Laurent normal-form statement; supporting localization definition.

proof.text:
Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$ be any affine open of $T$. The affine flatness criterion applied to $V\to X$ makes $C$ a flat $B$-algebra. Tensor the exact sequence of step 2 with $C$ over $B$ using flat tensor exactness. The canonical localization-tensor isomorphisms identify its three terms with $C$, $C_s\oplus C_t$, and $C_{st}$. Here the binary-sum identification is explicit: $(u,v)\otimes c\mapsto(u\otimes c,v\otimes c)$, with inverse the sum of the two summand inclusions. The maps become $c\mapsto(c,c)$ and $(a,b)\mapsto a-b$, because all comparisons send $c\otimes(b/s^n)$ to $cb/s^n$, and similarly for $t$ and $st$. We obtain
$$0\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow C_s\oplus C_t\longrightarrow C_{st}$$
exact at the first two terms. No finiteness or Noetherianity of $C$ has been used.

On $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$, the inverse image of $U$ is $D(s)\cup D(t)$: at a point the pulled-back section is invertible exactly when its image point lies in the corresponding principal open, since the map on local rings is local. Principal-open sections and their restriction maps identify the sheaf gluing equalizer for these two opens with $\ker(C_s\oplus C_t\to C_{st})$. Step 3 therefore says precisely that the canonical restriction $\mathcal O_T(V)\to\mathcal O_{U_T}(V\cap U_T)$ is an isomorphism. These are the components of the given sheaf map on the affine-open basis. Its local inverses glue uniquely: cover any open by affine opens, extend its restricted section on each, and use uniqueness on affine subopens of pairwise intersections to glue. Thus $\mathcal O_T\to(j_T)_*\mathcal O_{U_T}$ is an isomorphism, including on every open subset of $T$.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), parts (1), (3), (5); elementary sheaf gluing on D(s), D(t), with the comparison maps calculated in step 3.

proof.text: Choose an open cover $(V_i)$ trivializing both finite locally free modules, of ranks $m_i,n_i$. A homomorphism over $V_i\cap U_T$ is a matrix of $n_im_i$ functions: its columns are the images of the standard basis sections, which determine the sheaf map on every smaller open by linearity. Step 4 extends each entry uniquely to $V_i$, giving a homomorphism on $V_i$. On $V_i\cap V_j$ the two extensions agree: locally trivialize there and use injectivity for each matrix entry from step 4, since their restrictions to $U_T$ agree. The local homomorphisms thus glue, uniquely, to $M\to N$. The same entrywise injectivity shows that restriction is injective, proving its bijectivity. Ranks zero and ranks varying between opens cause no change.

source.place: Tag 01C6 (definition-locally-free); elementary matrix and sheaf gluing argument from the function isomorphism proved in step 4.

proof.text: Let $q:Z\to T$ be affine. For each affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $T$, write $q^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}D$. By the locally ringed space affine adjunction, sections over $V\cap U_T$ correspond to ring maps $D\to\Gamma(V\cap U_T,\mathcal O)$ whose composite with $C\to D$ is the structural map. Step 4 identifies this target ring with $C$ by the canonical restriction. Composing with its inverse therefore gives a unique $C$-algebra map $D\to C$, hence a unique section over $V$. The base condition holds because the inverse restriction sends the image of each $c\in C$ back to $c$. On overlaps the extensions agree on every affine subopen by the same uniqueness, so the sections glue. This proves both surjectivity and injectivity of restriction on sections. Empty opens and the zero ring are included by the same argument.

Step 1: lem-sfb-dvr-binomial-local-geometry with e=1 and (pi,s,t)=(s,t)=o, where D(s) and D(t) cover X minus o. It gives Noetherian, regular everywhere (local-ring form) and local dimension at most 2 with equality at o, so dim X=2 by lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings. X is integral because the Laurent normal form embeds B in K(T) (pi nonzero since a DVR is not a field), then spec-domain (2) applies. Step 2: the Laurent intersection equals the image of B and B_st embeds in K(T), so 0->B->B_s+B_t->B_st is exact; no surjectivity is claimed. Step 3: the affine flat criterion, flat tensor exactness and localization-tensor give the same sequence for every affine chart C, with no Noetherian hypothesis. Step 4: the tilde sections node identifies the two-open equalizer; affine-local bijectivity then glues to every open. Step 5: matrix entries extend by step 4, and entrywise injectivity gives agreement on overlaps. Step 6: q^{-1}V=Spec D; the adjunction applied to the non-affine source V intersect U_T, together with Gamma(V intersect U_T)=C, gives unique C-algebra maps D->C, which glue. Small cases: Z_(p) and k[[pi]] satisfy the hypotheses; Spec k at o is not flat and the conclusion fails there, so flatness is essential; empty and non-Noetherian T are covered. No Hartogs duplicate in the DAG. The unit route is unchanged. Accepted tool_use: lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings (generic dimension theory). Batch-5: lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base is a mathlib leaf (a polynomial ring over a regular ring is regular) and def-trf-strict-semistable-curve is a definition. Both are generic, outside the trace formula and Poincare duality and their proofs, so accepted. No SGA.
